audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gave Gnar four of seven stages including two-plus items, while Yorick wins 54.53% over 1414 games — the packet flags this contradiction directly. It also disagreed with the already-audited mirror on four rows.
audit.why: The late rows are backwards: Gnar has no wave clear and cannot duel a Maiden-plus-ghoul side lane, which is exactly why the win rate sits above 54%.
audit.corrected: Set to the mirror's chart — Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Gnar, Skill, Gnar, Yorick — as matched full/content pairs with ratings rescaled, and whys[3] and whys[6] restated so no row's prose contradicts its token. diffRating 8.5/10 to 6/10 with the two lines that quote the number updated.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike and cooldown line tracks 'GNAR!'s cooldown' as the thing to wait out.
audit.why: Mega Gnar is driven by the Rage bar, not by a spell cooldown — GNAR! (R) is only castable once he is already Mega. Waiting on an R cooldown tells you nothing about when the dangerous form arrives.
audit.corrected: Pointed the tracking at the Rage bar in dosFull[0].d and the mid paragraph, with Boomerang Throw's 16s and Hop's 22s rank-1 cooldowns as the concrete trade cues.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[2] warns you to avoid 'walls for Mega-E' — wrong ability, and it misses the interaction that actually matters. Its description body is unrelated boilerplate about trading without ghouls.
audit.why: Hop is the leap; the wall interaction belongs to GNAR! (R), which stuns and adds damage only to enemies thrown into a wall. Dark Procession creates terrain, so your own cage can be the wall he slams you into. Nothing on the page said this.
audit.corrected: Rewrote both the title and the body to state that your own wall arms his ultimate, and to never place the cage behind yourself.

audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 4-5 were sold as your window because 'the wall cages Mini Gnar'.
audit.why: Hop is a 475-range leap that clears terrain, so the cage does not trap Mini Gnar the way the page claimed.
audit.corrected: Restated as a stage he still controls, with the trade window defined as the gap after both Q and Hop are spent.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 8.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track GNAR! and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you read his Rage bar and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Hard matchup — difficulty 8.5/10, Gnar carry threat 8/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 6/10, Gnar carry threat 8/10.

edits.before: His Mega all-in. Don’t fight transform. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Mega comes off the Rage bar, not a cooldown — watch the bar and fight Mini.

edits.before: Trading without ghouls or caging nothing — Yorick without the swarm is the worst duelist in the lane.
edits.after: GNAR! only stuns on impact with a wall, and your own Dark Procession counts — never place the cage behind yourself.

edits.before: At levels 4-5 the Dark Procession wall cages Mini Gnar and your ghoul-plus-slow bursts beat his down Q.
edits.after: At levels 4-5 Hop leaps your wall and Boomerang Throw returns every 16s, so he still sets the spacing.

edits.before: In the 2+ item stage Gnar's ranged poke and Mega fights outscale you in lane, though your split-push is the real out.
edits.after: In the 2+ item stage your Maiden-and-ghoul split beats a Gnar with no wave clear, so make him answer the side lane.

edits.before: Gnar owns levels 1-2: his Boomerang Throw (Q) out-ranges your Last Rites and his Hyper passive shreds you before your ghouls stack, so eat the poke and just farm with Q resets.
edits.after: Gnar owns levels 1-2: Boomerang Throw out-ranges you at 1100 and halves its 16s cooldown when he catches it on the way back, so stand off the return path, eat the poke, and farm with Last Rites.

edits.before: The tide turns at 4-5 — your Dark Procession wall traps Mini Gnar, and with ghouls plus E-slow you win the short trade whenever his Q is on cooldown; keep him in Mini and punish the Rage gaps.
edits.after: At 4-5 he still sets the spacing: Hop is a 475-range leap that clears your wall on a 22s cooldown, and the boomerang returns every 16s. Trade only in the gap after both are spent, ghouls up, before the Rage bar fills.
